merger_description:
Baupost Group Securities, L.L.C. (**Baupost**) proposes to acquire a non-controlling, minority equity position in McDermott International, Ltd (**McDermott**) as part of an equity rights offering (the **Acquisition**).

Baupost is the nominee entity for The Baupost Group, L.L.C., a private hedge fund headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 1982. It manages a portfolio invested across a range of asset classes, including publicly traded debt and equity securities, private credit, private equity, and real estate investments. Its investments span a range of sectors, including technology, insurance and financial services, industrial distribution, and healthcare.

McDermott, established under the laws of Bermuda and headquartered in Houston, Texas, supplies engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction and installation (**EPCI**) solutions to the energy industry. It designs and builds end-to-end infrastructure solutions to transport and transform oil and gas into a variety of products. Its technologies, expertise and solutions, including in relation to energy transition, are utilised for offshore, subsea, LNG, and downstream energy projects globally. McDermott’s customers include national and major integrated oil and gas companies, as well as producers of petrochemicals and electric power. McDermott operates in over 30 countries, including most major energy-producing regions throughout the world, and has more than 30,000 employees.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationships
between Baupost and McDermott (or their connected entities) in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
